report.summary: Plan to address 8 reviewed findings: fix critical scoring stub, fragile SQL fallbacks, undefined constant; narrow unvalidated paths, arrival probe, error handling, determinism doc, WAL sidecars.
risks: If offset property is not implemented in any chunk of picker.py, scoring is broken and must be fixed.
If WIKI_RESOLVED is defined elsewhere in markdown.py, no change needed; but if missing, NameError on import.
String matching in ledger.py may mask other OperationalError conditions; replacement with error code check is fragile across SQLite versions.
Dynamic fallbacks may not exist in codebase; if they do, arrival probe and fallback evidence detection need updates.
todos: 1. Fix critical: Implement Candidate.offset in picker.py or verify existing implementation.
2. Fix critical: Define WIKI_RESOLVED in markdown.py or verify it's imported.
3. Fix high: Replace string match in ledger.py with error code check.
4. Fix high: Add explicit AttributeError handling in parse.py for ast.Index.
5. Fix medium: Add path validation in write_map and refresh_sources in maps.py.
6. Fix medium: Search for dynamic fallbacks; if found, update arrival probe and fallback detection.
7. Fix high: Create shared logging utility or ensure consistent error handling across evolution.py, imports.py, canary.py.
8. Fix low: Update docstring in bus.py to match sort key.
9. Fix low: Add comment in spine_ledger.py explaining WAL sidecar creation.

items.title: Implement or verify Candidate.offset property in picker.py
items.why_now: Critical: scoring is broken if offset is missing; this blocks the core scoring pipeline.

steps.do: Check if Candidate.offset is implemented in full picker.py: grep -n 'def offset' daedalus/spine/picker.py
steps.verified_by: If found, verify it returns a numeric value. If not, implement offset property returning 0 or appropriate value.

steps.do: If missing, add offset property to Candidate class.
steps.verified_by: Run pytest tests/test_picker.py::test_candidate_offset (assumes test exists) or write a quick test: assert candidate.offset is not None

items.assumption: The full picker.py file is available to check for existing implementation.

items.title: Define or import WIKI_RESOLVED in markdown.py
items.why_now: Critical: resolve_wiki_target will raise NameError if WIKI_RESOLVED is undefined, breaking wiki link resolution.

steps.do: Search entire markdown.py for WIKI_RESOLVED definition: grep -n 'WIKI_RESOLVED' daedalus/wiki/markdown.py
steps.verified_by: If not found, add definition: WIKI_RESOLVED = ... or import from appropriate module.

steps.do: If missing, add import or constant definition.
steps.verified_by: Run pytest tests/test_markdown.py::test_resolve_wiki_target (assumes test exists) or import module and check no NameError.

items.assumption: The constant WIKI_RESOLVED is not defined elsewhere in the module or imports.

items.title: Replace fragile string match in ledger.py with error code check
items.why_now: High: string matching on 'no such column' may mask other OperationalError conditions, leading to silent failures.

steps.do: Modify catch block in ledger.py to check sqlite3.OperationalError args for specific error code (e.g., err.args[0] == 'no such column' but use SQLite error code 1).
steps.verified_by: Run pytest tests/test_ledger.py::test_operational_error_handling (assumes test exists) or manual test: trigger OperationalError with different messages and verify only expected ones are caught.

items.assumption: SQLite error codes are consistent across versions.

items.title: Add explicit AttributeError handling in parse.py for ast.Index
items.why_now: High: getattr fallback returns wrong type on Python 3.9+, causing incorrect parsing.

steps.do: Modify parse.py to catch AttributeError when accessing ast.Index and handle appropriately (e.g., return None or raise a custom error).
steps.verified_by: Run pytest tests/test_parse.py::test_getattr_fallback (assumes test exists) or test on Python 3.9+ with code containing ast.Index.

items.assumption: The code uses ast.Index in a context where it may be absent in Python 3.9+.

items.title: Add path validation in write_map and refresh_sources in maps.py
items.why_now: Medium: unvalidated output paths could allow writing outside intended directory, posing security risk.

steps.do: Add check using os.path.commonpath to ensure output path is within a configurable base directory.
steps.verified_by: Write test: call write_map with path outside base dir and assert it raises ValueError or similar.

items.assumption: A base directory configuration exists or can be added.

items.title: Search for dynamic fallbacks and update arrival probe / fallback detection if needed
items.why_now: Medium: arrival probe and fallback evidence detection may miss dynamically set fallbacks, reducing monitoring accuracy.

steps.do: Search codebase for fallback set via function call or external config: grep -rn 'fallback' daedalus/ --include='*.py'
steps.verified_by: If any found, update arrival probe to detect them; else document that risk is theoretical.

steps.do: If dynamic fallbacks exist, modify arrival probe logic to include them.
steps.verified_by: Run existing tests to ensure no regression.

items.assumption: Dynamic fallbacks may exist; if none, no code change needed.

items.title: Create shared logging utility or ensure consistent error handling across evolution.py, imports.py, canary.py
items.why_now: High: inconsistent error handling can cause failures to go unnoticed, making debugging difficult.

steps.do: Check if shared logging utility exists: grep -rn 'import logging' daedalus/
steps.verified_by: If not, create a shared module (e.g., daedalus/common/logging.py) with a standard error handler.

steps.do: Update evolution.py, imports.py, canary.py to use the shared error handler.
steps.verified_by: Run tests for each module to ensure errors are logged consistently.

items.assumption: A shared logging utility is acceptable and does not introduce circular imports.

items.title: Update docstring in bus.py to match actual sort key
items.why_now: Low: documentation bug could mislead developers; fix is trivial.

steps.do: Modify docstring of append_round in bus.py to say 'sorted by (actor, role, status, canonical_body_json)' instead of 'sorted by actor id'.
steps.verified_by: Run grep -A5 'def append_round' daedalus/council/bus.py to verify docstring matches implementation.

items.assumption: The sort key is correct and intentional.

items.title: Add comment in SpineLedger explaining WAL sidecar creation
items.why_now: Low: minor documentation gap; prevents surprise for developers expecting zero disk writes.

steps.do: Add comment near the SQLite connection initialization in SpineLedger that WAL sidecar files are expected and harmless.
steps.verified_by: Visual inspection of the code comment.
